chapter_note: Core substrate is concentrated in ¶2–4 (and a definitional remnant in ¶1 and ¶8): Matter/Envy as a primordial Dark nature attacking key cosmic-historical figures (First Man; Image of the Ambassador; Adam). From ¶5 onward the chapter shifts into Christian/biographical/institutional application (Christ/cross; Mani and his church; catechumens; exhortation), matching the strong chapter-level editorial fatigue signal (pastoral drift in the second half).

paragraphs.core_text: [The] entirety of envy is this first nature that occu[red] in the worlds of darkness.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed dialogue/frame attribution: "Once again the apostle speaks to his disciples:" (compilation layer marker; "apostle"/disciples address).
paragraphs.temporal_note: Frame formula introduces a compact cosmological definition (envy as primordial Dark nature). Teaching voice becomes impersonal once the attribution is removed.

paragraphs.core_text: In this envy that [ ... ] in it, the First Man [ ... ] its poiso[n ... ] its evil-doing. His garment[s] were [ ... ] it cut them and drew them; [ ... ]
paragraphs.temporal_note: Cosmos→cosmos conflict report: Matter/Envy acting within the mythic system against the First Man (no institutional or audience address; no citation formulas).

paragraphs.core_text: It envied the first image of the Ambassador, which he displayed to it in the heights abov[e], i[n] his form that it saw. It established the seal and the image of flesh, and put the impression of t[h]at image on flesh, its very own birth.
paragraphs.temporal_note: System-internal mythic mechanism (Ambassador’s image; sealing/imprinting into flesh) stated as cosmological causation, not moral exhortation or church application.

paragraphs.core_text: [The th]ird time it envied Adam, the fir[st hum]an. It seized a power from him, and bore it forth from a [rib of] of Adam's [flesh].
paragraphs.temporal_note: Still written as internal myth-history (Matter seizing a power and generating from Adam’s flesh). The ‘rib’ motif suggests contact with Genesis tradition, but here it functions as a cosmological etiological detail rather than an explicit scriptural citation.
Explicit NT/Christian overlay markers: ‘blessed Christ’, ‘apostles’, ‘wood of the cross’—material entering via Christian narrative vocabulary rather than the impersonal cosmological register.

Biographical Mani-attribution and institutional anchoring (‘I… sent now’, ‘last generation’, ‘my… church’, ‘assembly of my catechumens’) shift the chapter into hagiographic/institutional application, consistent with editorial fatigue in the second half.

Application to communal life (sicknesses, rumors, accusations, hatred ‘among mankind’, attacks on ‘the teacher’ and ‘the righteous elect person’) maps the envy motif onto contemporary/social experience rather than staying within cosmic architecture.

paragraphs.core_text: This is the desire [of Mat]ter, the thought of death. This is the envy of its wi[cke]dness, that it casts upon the entire kindred of life from the very beginning
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed institutional/application material: the ‘fall from the faith’ passage and the historical anchoring ‘until my time, from m[e] too to my church.’ These pivot from cosmic description to community application.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Contains a brief impersonal definitional kernel (Matter’s desire = thought of death; envy cast upon the kindred of life) embedded within pastoral warning about negligence and an explicit ‘my time/my church’ anchor.
Pure exhortation/application voice (‘appropriate… wise person… steadfast… faith… hope’) with no cosmos→cosmos mapping; functions as moral admonition closing.
